{
  "skills": [
    {
      "skill_id": "polar_hbond_core_hydration_v3",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "heteroatom_dense_hydration",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_high"},
          "weight": 0.85,
          "rationale": "Dense O/N centers donate and accept multiple water hydrogen bonds, the dominant favorable hydration term."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "moderate_polar_support",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_mid"},
          "weight": 0.25,
          "rationale": "Intermediate polarity keeps coverage but is damped so it no longer dilutes the strongest polar stratum."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "saturated_hydrocarbon_cavity_penalty",
          "conditions": {"aromatic_bin": "aromatic_none", "hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_none"},
          "weight": -0.8,
          "rationale": "Apolar saturated solutes offer no hydrogen-bond sites; cavity formation cost dominates hydration free energy."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "polyhalogen_hydrophobic_penalty",
          "conditions": {"halogen_bin": "halogen_high"},
          "weight": -0.5,
          "rationale": "Heavily halogenated solutes are bulky, weakly hydrogen bonding, and typically poorly hydrated."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 1.3,
      "prior_scale": 0.6,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.5,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.18,
      "ucb_weight": 0.5,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.6,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.2,
      "gp_xi": 0.02,
      "confidence": 0.7,
      "hypothesis": "Hydration affinity tracks polar hydrogen-bonding surface; sharpening the hetero_high anchor and damping hetero_mid should restore top-end reach. Fails if the score rewards hydrophobic bulk or halogen polarizability."
    },
    {
      "skill_id": "ring_branch_role_transfer_length_downweight",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "polar_anchor_retained",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_high"},
          "weight": 0.6,
          "rationale": "Keeps the repeatedly useful polar hydrogen-bond anchor so the transferred role terms are tested, not confounded."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "ring_role_from_source_ring_bin",
          "conditions": {"ring_token_bin": "ring_token_low"},
          "weight": 0.35,
          "rationale": "Highest-transfer source role (ring_bin, weight 0.758); single rings with polar groups hydrate well."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "branch_role_from_rotatable_bonds",
          "conditions": {"branch_bin": "branch_mid"},
          "weight": 0.3,
          "rationale": "Source rotatable_bond role maps to branch tokens; branch points usually mark polar substituents in short SMILES."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "length_prior_downweighted",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_short"},
          "weight": -0.12,
          "rationale": "Counter-hypothesis: the low-confidence ESOL smiles_short bonus is downweighted and mildly reversed, since tiny alkanes hydrate poorly."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 1.0,
      "prior_scale": 0.45,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.4,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.15,
      "ucb_weight": 0.55,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.2,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.1,
      "gp_xi": 0.015,
      "confidence": 0.45,
      "hypothesis": "Transfers the two highest-weight source roles (ring, rotatable/branch) onto a damped polarity anchor while nearly nulling the uncertain length prior. Fails if ring and branch effects invert for hydration."
    }
  ],
  "selected_skill_id": "polar_hbond_core_hydration_v3",
  "lesson": "Across two development generations the mechanistic polarity skill led by roughly 15-23 AUC over length-prior skills in both literal and reversed forms, so length transfer is unreliable; broad hetero_mid weighting may have blunted top-end reach, warranting a sharper polar anchor.",
  "revision_summary": "Retained the winning polarity skill but damped hetero_mid, strengthened the hetero_high anchor and apolar penalties, and slightly reduced semantic mass to preserve exploration. Replaced the failed length-reversal skill with a role-transfer counter-hypothesis that carries the highest-weight source roles (ring, branch) on a damped polarity anchor while nearly nulling the uncertain length prior. Deployed the polarity skill."
}

rules.rationale: Dense O/N centers donate and accept multiple water hydrogen bonds, the dominant favorable hydration term.
Intermediate polarity keeps coverage but is damped so it no longer dilutes the strongest polar stratum.
Apolar saturated solutes offer no hydrogen-bond sites; cavity formation cost dominates hydration free energy.
Heavily halogenated solutes are bulky, weakly hydrogen bonding, and typically poorly hydrated.
